qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.mistake: The last FOL statement ∀x (p_2(x) ↔ p_3(x)) asserts that studying ancient cultures is equivalent to exploring new places for all x. The natural language statement says the same thing, so at first glance it seems correct. However, previous FOL-NL pairs already established a context: for example, ∀x (p_2(x) → p_3(x)) was presented as 'if x studies ancient cultures, then x explores new places', and ∀x (¬p_3(x) → ¬p_2(x)) as the contrapositive. But now saying they are fully equivalent (↔) adds a reverse implication (if x explores new places, then x studies ancient cultures), which was not previously implied or necessarily intended. However, the **pair in isolation** — just this FOL and this NL — is correctly matched: ↔ does mean 'if and only if', and the NL correctly reflects that. So why False?
